what_it_does: On tiny embedded devices (like IoT sensors), a program declares variables as 32-bit integers even when they only use 8 bits in practice, wasting energy. BitSpec is a compiler-hardware partnership that reduces variable widths to match actual runtime needs. The compiler predicts smaller bit-widths and uses speculative narrow instructions. When a value exceeds the narrow range, hardware reports the overflow and software re-executes with the original safe width. This captures energy savings in the common case while maintaining correctness.
